defects: Hypothesis is stronger than gold's: `(l.filter p).length ≤ 1` requires at most one *list element* (counted with multiplicity) to satisfy p, whereas gold's `{x ∈ l₁ | p x}.Subsingleton` only requires the *set* of values satisfying p to have at most one distinct element, permitting duplicate occurrences of that same value. E.g. l = [a, a, b] with p a = true, p b = false satisfies gold's hypothesis (set {a} is a subsingleton) but not the produced one (filter length = 2), so the produced theorem is strictly weaker and does not cover all cases the gold theorem does.
